temp.title: Temporary files and caches
temp.description: Windows, your browsers and apps recreate them on their own
temp.what: Scratch files and caches that Windows, browsers and apps write while they work. Only files untouched for over a day are included, so nothing in use is touched.
temp.ifRemoved: Nothing you would notice: apps recreate what they need. Some pages or games may open a little slower the first time.

installers.title: Installers already used
installers.description: Setup files in Downloads for programs you already installed
installers.what: Setup files in Downloads for programs that are already installed on this PC.
installers.ifRemoved: Nothing: the programs stay installed. To reinstall one, download it again.

oldDownloads.title: Old downloads
oldDownloads.description: In your Downloads folder, not opened in over a year
oldDownloads.what: Files in Downloads you have not opened or changed in over a year.
oldDownloads.ifRemoved: They might still matter (a receipt, a document): look at the list before removing them.

duplicates.title: Duplicates
duplicates.description: Identical copies: the oldest one is always kept
duplicates.ifRemoved: You keep one copy of each file, so nothing is lost. Links or shortcuts to the removed copy will no longer open it.

largeFiles.title: Large files
largeFiles.description: Files of 1 GB or more in your folders
largeFiles.what: Files of 1 GB or more in your folders: videos, disk images, backups.
largeFiles.ifRemoved: They are often personal: check each one before removing it.

recycleBin.title: Recycle Bin
recycleBin.description: Items in the Recycle Bin for more than 30 days
recycleBin.what: Files you deleted more than 30 days ago that are still in the Recycle Bin. Newer ones stay, in case you change your mind.
recycleBin.ifRemoved: It is like emptying the Recycle Bin, but only for these old items.

crashReports.title: Error reports and dumps
crashReports.description: Created by Windows when an app crashes
crashReports.what: Reports and memory dumps Windows writes when an app crashes, to help developers find the problem.
crashReports.ifRemoved: Nothing changes for you: they are only useful to someone investigating an old crash.

thumbnails.title: Thumbnail cache
thumbnails.description: Photo and video previews File Explorer recreates on its own
thumbnails.what: Small previews of your photos and videos that File Explorer keeps so folders open quickly.
thumbnails.ifRemoved: Previews take a moment to appear the next time you open a folder. Files Explorer is using right now are left in place.

unknownFolders.title: Unknown folders
unknownFolders.description: Big folders in AppData and ProgramData: find out what they are
unknownFolders.what: Big folders apps keep in AppData and ProgramData. The app explains the ones it knows; tap a folder to find out what it is.
unknownFolders.ifRemoved: Move them one at a time, after reading what they are: the whole group cannot be selected, because many belong to apps you still use.

explain.title: What is this?
explain.source: Explanation built into the app · no data sent
explain.unknownHint: A folder is usually named after the app or company that made it. If you don't recognise it, leave it where it is.

temp.label: Temporary files
temp.what: Scratch files Windows and apps write while they work, then usually forget to delete.
temp.ifRemoved: Nothing you would notice: apps create new ones when they need them.

inetCache.label: Internet cache
inetCache.what: Copies of web pages and images saved by Windows and older apps to open them faster.
inetCache.ifRemoved: Some pages may load a little slower the first time.

browserCache.label: Browser cache
browserCache.what: Images and files of websites your browser keeps so pages open faster. Your passwords, bookmarks and history are not here.
browserCache.ifRemoved: Websites load a bit slower the first time, then the browser saves them again.

browserData.label: Browser data
browserData.what: Your browser's profile: bookmarks, saved passwords, history, extensions and settings, plus its caches.
browserData.ifRemoved: You would lose bookmarks, passwords and settings that are not synced to an account.

shaderCache.label: Graphics card cache
shaderCache.what: Ready-made graphics instructions (shaders) for games and apps, so they start without stutter.
shaderCache.ifRemoved: Games may stutter a little the first time you play them again, then the cache is rebuilt.

crashDumps.label: Error reports
crashDumps.what: Reports and memory dumps Windows writes when an app crashes, to help developers find the problem.
crashDumps.ifRemoved: Nothing changes for you. Only developers looking into an old crash would miss them.

thumbCache.label: Thumbnail cache
thumbCache.what: Small previews of your photos and videos that File Explorer saves so folders open quickly.
thumbCache.ifRemoved: The first time you open a folder with many photos, previews take a moment to appear again.

recycleBin.label: Recycle Bin
recycleBin.what: Files you deleted. Windows keeps them here in case you change your mind.
recycleBin.ifRemoved: They are gone for good, as when you empty the Recycle Bin.

windowsData.label: Windows data
windowsData.what: Settings and data of Windows and Microsoft apps (Office, Teams, OneDrive, Edge and others).
windowsData.ifRemoved: Windows features or Microsoft apps may stop working properly.

storeApps.label: Microsoft Store apps
storeApps.what: Data of the apps installed from the Microsoft Store, each in its own folder.
storeApps.ifRemoved: Those apps would lose their data or stop working. To free space, uninstall the app from the Apps screen instead.

userPrograms.label: Installed programs
userPrograms.what: Programs installed only for you, such as Visual Studio Code, Python or GitHub Desktop.
userPrograms.ifRemoved: Those programs would stop working. Uninstall them from the Apps screen instead.

packageCache.label: Installer copies
packageCache.what: Copies of the installers Windows keeps to repair, update or uninstall programs such as Visual Studio and .NET.
packageCache.ifRemoved: Some programs may no longer update or uninstall correctly.

gpuDrivers.label: Graphics drivers
gpuDrivers.what: Files of your graphics card driver and its control panel, sometimes with copies of past driver installers.
gpuDrivers.ifRemoved: The graphics driver or its settings app may stop working.

discord.label: Discord app
discord.what: The Discord app itself and its settings, updates and cache.
discord.ifRemoved: Discord would stop working. If you no longer use it, uninstall it from the Apps screen.

spotify.label: Spotify music and cache
spotify.what: Songs you downloaded for offline listening and Spotify's cache of recently played music.
spotify.ifRemoved: Downloaded songs need to be downloaded again; Spotify itself keeps working.

zoom.label: Zoom app
zoom.what: The Zoom app, which installs itself here, and its settings.
zoom.ifRemoved: Zoom would stop working. If you no longer use it, uninstall it from the Apps screen.

slack.label: Slack app
slack.what: The Slack app, its updates and its cache.
slack.ifRemoved: Slack would stop working. If you no longer use it, uninstall it from the Apps screen.

telegram.label: Telegram app
telegram.what: The Telegram desktop app, your login and the photos and videos it downloaded.
telegram.ifRemoved: You would be logged out and downloaded media would be gone from this PC.

whatsapp.label: WhatsApp app
whatsapp.what: The WhatsApp desktop app and the media it saved.
whatsapp.ifRemoved: WhatsApp would stop working on this PC.

vscode.label: VS Code data
vscode.what: Settings, extension data and caches of Visual Studio Code.
vscode.ifRemoved: You would lose your VS Code settings and open work, unless Settings Sync is on.

devCache.label: Developer tool cache
devCache.what: Packages downloaded by developer tools (npm, pip, Yarn, NuGet) to install them faster next time.
devCache.ifRemoved: The next install downloads them again.

npmGlobal.label: Developer tools
npmGlobal.what: Command line tools installed with npm for the whole user.
npmGlobal.ifRemoved: Those tools would stop working until installed again.

jetbrains.label: JetBrains data
jetbrains.what: Settings, caches and indexes of JetBrains IDEs; with Toolbox, the IDEs themselves too.
jetbrains.ifRemoved: Caches are rebuilt, but settings and IDEs installed by Toolbox would be lost.

docker.label: Docker data
docker.what: Docker Desktop's virtual disk with your images, containers and volumes.
docker.ifRemoved: Docker would lose every image, container and volume. Use Docker's own clean up instead.

steamCache.label: Steam cache
steamCache.what: Web pages and images of the Steam store and library, kept to show them faster.
steamCache.ifRemoved: Steam downloads them again. Your games are not here.

epicGames.label: Epic Games data
epicGames.what: Settings of the Epic Games Launcher and the list of the games it installed.
epicGames.ifRemoved: The launcher may no longer find your installed games.

minecraft.label: Minecraft worlds
minecraft.what: Minecraft Java Edition: your worlds, saves, mods and resource packs.
minecraft.ifRemoved: Your worlds would be lost for good.

iphoneBackup.label: iPhone backups
iphoneBackup.what: Backups of your iPhone or iPad made by iTunes or Apple Devices, plus their settings.
iphoneBackup.ifRemoved: You could no longer restore your phone from these backups. Delete old backups from iTunes or Apple Devices instead.

adobe.label: Adobe data
adobe.what: Settings, presets and caches of Adobe apps; the media cache of Premiere and After Effects can get big.
adobe.ifRemoved: Caches are rebuilt, but presets, fonts and settings could be lost. Clear the media cache from the app's preferences.

updaterLeftovers.label: Update leftovers
updaterLeftovers.what: Temporary files left by the updater many apps use (Discord, Teams, Slack and others).
updaterLeftovers.ifRemoved: Nothing: apps create it again during their next update.

packageManagers.label: Package manager
packageManagers.what: Chocolatey or Scoop and the programs they installed.
packageManagers.ifRemoved: Programs installed with them would stop working or could no longer be updated.
